description_full: Avino Silver & Gold Mines Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the acquisition, exploration, and advancement of mineral properties in Mexico. It explores for silver, gold, copper, and base metal deposits. The company holds 100% interest in the Avino Mine area property covering an area of approximately 4,086.93 hectares comprising 42 mineral claims and leases 4 mineral claims, which is located in the state of Durango, Mexico. It also has an option to acquire 100% interest in the Ana Maria and El Laberinto properties located in Mexico. The company was formerly known as International Avino Mines Ltd. and changed its name to Avino Silver & Gold Mines Ltd. in August 1997. Avino Silver & Gold Mines Ltd. was incorporated in 1968 and is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada.

The top line has compounded at +81% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at -1% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 37× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 6.3% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
